nist_epq.terms: NIST-authored work; public domain in the United States. Retain the upstream notice. The notice also disclaims warranties and asks that derived works not imply NIST endorsement.
nist_epq.citation: NIST DTSA-II/EPQ; BergerSeltzerBrem pdebr tables. The table comments trace the underlying data to Seltzer and Berger.
nist_epq.transformation: For every element and native incident energy, construct the 32-node CeeLo grid uniformly: kappa=0.025 is quadratic Lagrange interpolation through EPQ kappa={0,0.05,0.1}; kappa=0.075 is cubic Lagrange interpolation through EPQ kappa={0,0.05,0.1,0.15}; all other output nodes are copied from equal-kappa EPQ nodes and EPQ kappa=0.125 is omitted. Select the 27 native energies from 10 keV through 20 MeV. No row normalization is applied; phi_rad is a validation checksum only. Quantize each element's complete table to uint16 with one float32 scale; the generator reports row, integrated-rate, and mean-kappa packing error.
nist_epq.provenance_caveat: PENELOPE-2008 describes its related 32-node database as supplied by S. Seltzer. No independently redistributable copy of the later PENELOPE/Geant4 low-kappa revision is used. This general interpolation of public-domain EPQ data was validated against aggregate/numerical Geant4 behavior; it is not a transcription or fitted reproduction of G4EMLOW coefficients.

epdl2023.terms: Openly distributed by the IAEA Nuclear Data Services EPICS project; retain source and evaluation citations.
epdl2023.citation: EPICS2023 EPDL; D.E. Cullen et al., UCRL-50400 Vol. 6 Rev. 5 and EPICS2023 release materials.
epdl2023.transformation: Use incident energies from 10 keV through the historical 10 MeV upper bound. Retain endpoints, process thresholds, and explicit lower-flank/upper-edge pairs at duplicated absorption edges. Treat all other native EPDL nodes as mandatory validation probes rather than mandatory retained coefficients; also test 16 logarithmic positions per retained interval and adaptively insert the worst failing point. Rayleigh total cross sections use one jointly refined float32 log-energy grid for each group of four adjacent elements; every element in a group must independently pass the unchanged pointwise and integrated gates. Other photon-process coordinates are uint16 indices into one bit-exact deduplicated float32 log-coordinate pool. Encode every log-value with per-curve affine uint16 packing; compact descriptors store integer offsets rather than pointers. No decoded or contiguous raw photon-grid compatibility views are retained. The generator validates the decoded runtime representation to 0.1% pointwise and 0.05% integrated error (0.05% pointwise for pair production). The incoherent scattering-function tables retain x>=0.01 inverse angstrom and use flat offset-addressed float32 coordinate arrays and packed values. Form-factor curves are adaptively reconstructed and validated inside the generator but are not emitted as runtime lookup tables. Generate each element's 256-node normalized Rayleigh sampling CDF offline from that validated form-factor curve and store it as uint16 on one shared float32 x grid. Gate angular behavior against EPDL down to x=1e-7 at 0.25% CDF and 0.002 mean-cosine error, uint16 CDF quantization at 8e-6 absolute error, and the complete sampling representation at 0.25% against dense integration.

eadl2023.terms: Openly distributed by the IAEA Nuclear Data Services EPICS project; retain source and evaluation citations.
eadl2023.citation: EPICS2023 EADL; S.T. Perkins et al., UCRL-50400 Vol. 30.
eadl2023.transformation: Retain K, L1, L2, and L3 relaxation data through Z=99 so radioactive-decay daughters are covered beyond the Z=92 transport-table limit. Store radiative yields, line energies and normalized line probabilities in variable-length per-subshell arrays rather than fixed 24-line slots; retain Coster-Kronig L-vacancy transfer probabilities. L photons below the 10 keV transport cut are omitted and their probability is not reassigned to retained lines.

eedl2023.description: EPICS2023 Evaluated Electron Data Library (independent bremsstrahlung validation only)
eedl2023.terms: Openly distributed by the IAEA Nuclear Data Services EPICS project; retain source and evaluation citations.
eedl2023.citation: EPICS2023 EEDL; S.T. Perkins, D.E. Cullen and S.M. Seltzer, UCRL-50400 Vol. 31.

nist_star.description: NIST STAR downloadable source package containing ESTAR
nist_star.terms: NIST permits redistribution and modification of the downloadable programs and database, provided the original NIST notices are retained and modifications are clearly identified.
nist_star.citation: M.J. Berger et al., ESTAR/PSTAR/ASTAR, NIST Standard Reference Database 124; M.J. Berger and S.M. Seltzer, NBSIR 82-2550.
nist_star.transformation: The downloadable program and FEDAT database are the locked algorithm/database provenance. The generated elemental values are obtained from NIST's official ESTAR text interface, which runs the same ESTAR calculation, for every element Z=1..92. Retain all 53 standard-grid energy nodes from 10 keV through 20 MeV. Generated tables are marked as derived from NIST ESTAR; the web output is rounded by NIST to four significant figures (the upstream source says the calculation is accurate to approximately three).

nist_estar_text.description: Official NIST ESTAR elemental text tables generated from SRD 124
nist_estar_text.logical_hash_definition: For Z=1..92 in order, SHA-256 over little-endian uint16 Z followed by little-endian float64 triples (energy_MeV, collision_MeV_cm2_g, radiative_MeV_cm2_g) for the 53 rows from 0.01 through 20 MeV.
nist_estar_text.terms: NIST permits redistribution and modification of the downloadable programs and database, provided the original NIST notices are retained and modifications are clearly identified.
nist_estar_text.citation: M.J. Berger et al., ESTAR/PSTAR/ASTAR, NIST Standard Reference Database 124; M.J. Berger and S.M. Seltzer, NBSIR 82-2550.
nist_estar_text.transformation: Parse collision and radiative mass stopping powers at every official standard-grid node from 10 keV through 20 MeV and convert energy to keV. For each element and each stopping process, take base-10 logarithms and encode the complete 53-node row with one float32 offset, one float32 scale, and uint16 coefficients. No element or energy interpolation occurs during generation. Runtime decoding precedes linear interpolation in log10(E) and log10(stopping power); the generator reports the added packing error at every native node.

xraylib.terms: BSD-3-Clause; retain the copyright and disclaimer notices in the upstream source distribution.
xraylib.citation: T. Schoonjans et al., Spectrochimica Acta Part B 66 (2011) 776-784.
xraylib.transformation: For each occupied subshell, store electron occupancy, binding energy, and the per-electron partial Compton profile J(0). These drive the existing PENELOPE-style analytic impulse-approximation profile; they are independent of G4EMLOW.
